correctness.rationale: Any affine h(x)=cx+d minorizing a x^2/2 satisfies d<=-c^2/(2a); for fixed c the tangent envelope maximizes distance to the target sublevel, reducing the supremum to tangents h_y. For 0<Delta<G and u>0 the relevant slopes are y>0, with target distance d_y=u-y/2-y_*^2/(2y) and exact loss d_{y_*}-d_y=(y-y_*)^2/(2y), proving the unique optimizer y_*=u sqrt(1-r). At Delta=G, y->0+ approaches but never attains the supremum; at Delta>G, h=0 has empty target and infinite slowness under the source convention. Substitution into the W inequality gives the stated necessary-and-sufficient trial-modulus frontier. Symmetry restores |u|.
risks: One-dimensional unconstrained geometry only; no claim that a bundle algorithm generates the globally optimal affine minorant.

value.rationale: The trial growth modulus is a central adaptive quantity of the new W-certificate framework, and the scalar strongly convex quadratic is its canonical exact-growth benchmark. A complete necessary-and-sufficient inflation frontier, including the sharp nonattainment at the true gap/modulus, gives a motivated boundary fact about what the certificate can geometrically achieve; it is more than a numerical example or routine verification of a single parameter choice.
risks: The scientific value is calibration of a new certificate, not a general multidimensional optimization theorem.

limitations: One-dimensional unconstrained scalar quadratic only; higher-dimensional anisotropy, constraints, and actual bundle-generation dynamics remain open.
